title: Longest Alternating Subarray
notes:
## Intuition

An alternating subarray is pinned down by where it starts: its first two values must be `x` and `x + 1`, and every later value must equal the one two places before it. With at most 100 numbers, you can simply try every start and stretch the subarray as far as the pattern allows. (Checking every start and end pair separately also works, but it repeats the same comparisons.)

## Approach

1. Set `best = -1` for "no alternating subarray yet".
2. For each `start`, skip it unless `nums[start + 1]` is exactly `nums[start] + 1`.
3. Otherwise set `end = start + 1` and move `end` right while the next value equals `nums[end - 1]`, the value two places back.
4. The run `start..end` has length `end - start + 1`; keep the largest in `best`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2,3,4,3,4]`.

- `start = 0`: `3 - 2 = 1`, so `end = 1`. The next value `4` is not `nums[0] = 2`, so the run is `[2,3]` and `best = 2`.
- `start = 1`: `4 - 3 = 1`, so `end = 2`. `nums[3] = 3` equals `nums[1]`, so `end = 3`; `nums[4] = 4` equals `nums[2]`, so `end = 4`. The run `[3,4,3,4]` has length 4, so `best = 4`.
- `start = 2`: `3 - 4 = -1`, skipped.
- `start = 3`: `4 - 3 = 1`, run `[3,4]` of length 2.

The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each start can stretch across the rest of the array.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- The first step must go **up** by exactly one: `[4,3]` is not alternating, though `[3,4,3]` is.
- A pair like `[1,3,1,3]` switches between two values but differs by 2, so it does not count.
- Return `-1`, not `0` or `1`, when no pair `x, x + 1` exists.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | longest alternating length found so far, or `-1` |
| `start` | index where the candidate subarray begins |
| `end` | last index the current run reaches |

narration.2: No alternating subarray has been found yet, which is also the answer if none exists.
narration.3: Try each index that still has a neighbour to its right as the start.
narration.4: An alternating subarray must begin with a step of exactly +1.
narration.5: Not here, so move on to the next start.
narration.7: The first two elements form a valid run that ends at start + 1.
narration.8: Extend while the next value repeats the value two places back, keeping the up/down pattern.
narration.9: The pattern holds, so the run grows by one.
narration.11: Record the length of this run if it is the longest so far.
narration.13: Return the longest run, or -1 if every start was skipped.
